{{Quote|The lightsaber pike employs the same combat style as the dual-bladed saber. Both are staff weapons, but the pike has a shaft of saber-resistant metal, and a short blade on only one end.|[[Skarch Vaunk]] entry on lightsaber pikes in ''[[The Jedi Path: A Manual for Students of the Force]]''|<ref name="The Jedi Path">[[The Jedi Path: A Manual for Students of the Force (real-life book)|''The Jedi Path: A Manual for Students of the Force'']]</ref>}}
The '''lightsaber pike''', also known as the '''lightsaber lance''', was a unique weapon that resembled a primitive halberd or spear in many aspects. As staff weapons, they were typically considered the domain of [[Jedi Weapon Master|exotic weapon specialists]] among the Jedi. They were notably used by all [[Jedi Temple Guard/Legends|Jedi Temple Guards]] during the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]].

Many members of the [[Knights of Zakuul]], the enforcers of justice in the [[Eternal Empire]], were also users of these weapons.

==Description==
[[File:NexusOfPower_Front_FG_art.png|thumb|left|250px|A Jedi Temple Guard wielding a double-bladed lightsaber pike]]
There were two different forms of lightsaber pike, with the first being much like a spear, glaive, or other, similar polearms. Its [[Long-handle lightsaber|long handle]] was made of a lightsaber-resistant material; [[Phrik/Legends|phrik]] alloy being a prime choice.<ref name="JATM" /><ref name="The Jedi Path" /> At the end of the handle was a [[Lightsaber/Legends|lightsaber]] blade that was shorter and thicker than a normal one.<ref name="TFUn">[[Star Wars: The Force Unleashed (novelization)|''Star Wars: The Force Unleashed'' novelization]]</ref> The blade could be activated by a switch further down the weapon's shaft. Including the blade, the weapon was almost as long as the wielder's body and could keep enemies at a distance, giving the advantage of a longer reach.<ref name="JATM" /> A similar weapon was the [[Cortosis staff/Legends|cortosis staff]] used by the [[Morgukai]].

The second type of lightsaber pike sported another blade at the other end<ref name="The Wrong Jedi" /> and to all appearances seemed identical in both form and function to a [[Double-bladed lightsaber/Legends|double-bladed lightsaber]], with which it shared a "nearly identical" combat style.<ref name="The Jedi Path" /> The most prominent examples of this model were used by the [[Jedi Temple Guard/Legends|Jedi Temple Guards]], which had yellow blades that appeared relatively shorter than the ones found on a double-bladed lightsaber.

==History==
[[File:KnightsofZakuul.png|thumb|220x220px|Knights of Zakuul, wielding lightsaber pikes.]]
In the time of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Old Republic]], both the [[Sith Empire (Post–Great Hyperspace War)|Sith Empire]] and the Republic were overwhelmed by the sudden [[Eternal Empire raids|reveal]] and subsequent [[Eternal Empire conquest|invasion]] of the [[Eternal Empire]] of the planet [[Zakuul]]. Among the forces from Zakuul were the famed [[Knights of Zakuul]] who had sworn to guard the [[Tenebrae|Emperor of the Eternal Throne]] and his family. The knights were [[Force-sensitive/Legends|Force-sensitive]] and used a wide range of lightsaber weapons, the most prominent of which was the lightsaber pike. These pikes were often used along with a [[Blaster/Legends|blaster]] bolt reflective shield.<ref name="KOTFE" />

[[File:Arkanians_DoH.png|thumb|left|249x249px|Two Arkanians, one wielding a lightsaber pike.]]
[[Millennium/Legends|Millennia]] after the [[Battle of Zakuul|fall of Zakuul]], a different model of lightsaber pike was the trademark weapons of the [[Jedi Temple Guard/Legends|Jedi Temple Guards]] during the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]]. These pikes were a variation of double-bladed lightsaber, each emitting yellow blades.<ref name="The Wrong Jedi" /> Following the Clone Wars and [[Order 66/Legends|Order 66]], the Jedi [[Kazdan Paratus]] wielded a [[Kazdan Paratus's lightsaber pike|lightsaber pike]]<ref name="TFUn" /> closer in design to those used by the Knights of Zakuul<ref name="KOTFE" />, taking the weapon into exile with him on [[Raxus Prime/Legends|Raxus Prime]] during the [[Great Jedi Purge/Legends|Great Jedi Purge]]. When the Aleena Jedi built his mechanical legs to move around in haste, his lightsaber pike was the requirement for his mechanical arms to use with deadly precision. He ultimately wielded it against [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader's]] [[Sith apprentice/Legends|apprentice]], [[Galen Marek|Starkiller]], and the weapon was destroyed in the ensuing melee. After he attempted to fix it in [[Meditation/Legends|meditation]], Starkiller realized that his lightsaber [[Lightsaber crystal/Legends|focusing crystal]] lens were damaged, so they could not be realigned and thus the pike was discarded.<ref name="TFUn" />

During this time, lightsaber pikes were also the favored weapons of the [[Emperor's Shadow Guard]], elite guards with minor knowledge of the Force and lightsaber-wielding skills. Starkiller fought several of these elite guards, once on [[Bespin/Legends|Bespin]] as he attempted to rescue the Jedi [[Rahm Kota/Legends|Rahm Kota]], and also on Raxus Prime when he returned to [[Second mission to Raxus Prime|destroy]] an [[Imperial-class Star Destroyer/Legends|Imperial Star Destroyer]] [[Shipyard/Legends|shipyard]] so as to eliminate a source of fear and gain the confidence of others. Saber Pikes also saw occasional use by the [[Emperor's Royal Guard/Legends|Emperor's Royal Guard]] and the [[Imperial Senate Guard/Legends|Imperial Senate Guard]].<ref name="TFUvg" />

==Behind the scenes==
[[File:LightsaberPikeConcept.png|thumb|right|150px|Concept art by [[Carlos Sanchez]], dated [[September]] [[2011]]]]
The lightsaber pike first appeared in [[Star Wars: The Force Unleashed (novelization)|''The Force Unleashed'']], a novel written by [[Sean Williams]]<ref name="The Force Unleashed novel">[[Star Wars: The Force Unleashed (novelization)|''Star Wars: The Force Unleashed'' novelization]] novel</ref> that was released on [[August 19]], [[2008]]<ref name="The Force Unleashed novel release date">{{RandomHouseOld|url=catalog/display.pperl?isbn=9780345499028|text=Star Wars(r) The Force Unleashed}}</ref> as part of the ''[[Star Wars: The Force Unleashed]]'' multimedia project.<ref name="The Force Unleashed multimedia project">''[[Star Wars: The Force Unleashed]]'' multimedia project</ref> Kazdan Paratus wields a blue lightsaber pike in the [[Wikipedia:Xbox 360|Xbox 360]] and [[Wikipedia:PlayStation 3|PlayStation 3]] versions of the game, but a yellow lightsaber pike in the [[Wikipedia:Nintendo DS|Nintendo DS]] version, and a yellow [[Double-bladed lightsaber/Legends|double-bladed lightsaber]] with an elongated hilt in the [[Wikipedia:Wii|Wii]], [[Wikipedia:PlayStation 2|PlayStation 2]], and [[Wikipedia:PlayStation Portable|PlayStation Portable]] versions. The novelization also describes his lightsaber staff as having two blades, one significantly shorter than the other.

In the planning stages of "[[The Wrong Jedi]]," the lightsaber pikes carried by the Jedi Temple Guards were originally to have green blades. However, they later became yellow.<ref name="The Wrong Jedi Trivia Gallery">{{SW|url=series/clone-wars/the-wrong-jedi-trivia-gallery|text="The Wrong Jedi" Trivia Gallery}}</ref>

It is unknown why the weapons used by the Temple Guards are called "pikes" since they are all but identical to a double-bladed lightsaber in both form and function, and the name had previously been used to refer to an actual polearm.

===Sith warrior lightsaber pike===
[[File:Sith_warrior_lightsaber_pike_bts.jpg|thumb|right|200px|Unused concept art of Darth Bane's lightsaber pike, from ''The Clone Wars'' episode "Sacrifice"]]
A single-bladed lightsaber pike dubbed the "Sith warrior lightsaber pike" was designed<ref name="Sith lightsaber pike">{{SW|url=series/clone-wars/sacrifice-concept-art-gallery|text="Sacrifice" Concept Art Gallery}} {{C|Slide 3}}</ref> for use by [[Darth Bane/Legends|Darth Bane]] in "[[Sacrifice (episode)|Sacrifice]],"<ref name="Darth Bane">{{SW|url=series/clone-wars/sacrifice-concept-art-gallery|text="Sacrifice" Concept Art Gallery}}</ref> the thirteenth episode of the animated series ''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars]]''{{'}} [[The Clone Wars: The Lost Missions|sixth season]], though it didn't appear in the episode's final cut.<ref name="Sacrifice">{{TCW|Sacrifice (episode)}}</ref>
